headline: A Russian Geran-4 loitering munition equipped with an electro-optical (EO) seeker struck a Ukrainian helicopter at Zhuliany Airport in Kyiv on September 4. The helicopter is claimed to have been a UH-60 Black Hawk operated by Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR/GUR). There is no visual confirmation of the strike itself. However, earlier satellite imagery shows a UH-60 parked at the exact location, while a subsequent low-resolution satellite image shows a distinct black burn mark at the site. Ukrainian sources reported the attack but claimed that decommissioned Yak-40 passenger aircraft were hit instead.
summary: A Russian Geran-4 loitering munition equipped with an electro-optical (EO) seeker struck a Ukrainian helicopter at Zhuliany Airport in Kyiv on September 4. The helicopter is claimed to have been a UH-60 Black Hawk operated by Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR/GUR).

headline: Video circulating on Telegram appears to show the immediate aftermath of an apparent drone strike on the Panama flagged very large crude carrier (VLCC) New Andros in Iraqi territorial waters at approximately 6:00 a.m. local time today. Iraqi port officials told Reuters that the tanker, which was carrying roughly 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil, was struck by a drone and caught fire. Iraqi rescue boats responded and extinguished the fire. All 22 crew members aboard were reported safe, with no casualties and no reported oil leakage. The identity of the drone or the party responsible for the attack has not been officially established. The incident comes amid a major escalation in attacks on commercial shipping across the Gulf following recent U.S. strikes on Iranian tankers and Iran’s subsequent threats against maritime traffic. headline: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Center has issued two advisories following reports of suspected attacks on commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. headline: NTSB officials provided the final on scene press briefing tonight on the investigation into the runway excursion of 21 Air Flight 7598 at Miami International Airport on Sunday, which left five people dead and five others injured. The Boeing 767 cargo aircraft overran the end of Runway 30 while landing after a flight from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Investigators said data from the final 30 seconds of the flight data recorder shows the crew released the brakes and increased engine power to a level consistent with initiating a go around for approximately four seconds before reapplying the brakes, which remained applied through the end of the recording. The NTSB expects the on scene phase of the investigation to continue for approximately one week as investigators collect additional evidence and conduct interviews. A preliminary report is expected within 30 days, while the full investigation and final report could take more than a year.

headline: U.S. Southern Command has released video showing Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTF-WHEM) forces interdicting and destroying a floating refueling station allegedly supporting narco-trafficking operations in the Eastern Pacific. According to SOUTHCOM, U.S. forces boarded and cleared the vessel, removed the personnel aboard and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities before sinking the vessel. Intelligence reportedly linked the refueling station to Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian criminal organization designated by the U.S. as a foreign terrorist organization. This is the second operation of this type. JTF-WHEM conducted a similar interdiction on Aug. 28, when Marines and Sailors operating from USS San Antonio (LPD 17) boarded a suspected floating refueling station, removed those aboard, transferred them to Ecuador and then sank the vessel. The video released by SOUTHCOM today shows what appears to be the USS San Antonio operating nearby. The latest operation is part of an increasingly active U.S.-Ecuadorian campaign targeting the maritime logistics network supporting drug trafficking in the Eastern Pacific.
